whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Platform Foundations exam for?

personas.label: People new to Salesforce
personas.description: You have used Salesforce for a few months and want to earn your first Salesforce credential.

personas.label: People exploring a new career
personas.description: You are considering CRM work and want to learn the basics employers expect.

personas.label: Salesforce business users
personas.description: You use Salesforce in sales, service, or operations and want to show what you know.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Platform Foundations Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam covers many parts of Salesforce at an introductory level. You will need a broad overview of the data model, products, access, reports, automation, and the Salesforce ecosystem.
bullets: 62% to pass, or about 25 correct answers out of 40. Check the current exam guide before booking.
Many topics, basic detail. Expect a little about each area rather than deep questions on one topic.
Learn the exact terms. Several answer choices may sound reasonable, so know what each feature is called and does.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You are ready when you can describe the standard objects, explain the difference between Salesforce clouds, and tell profiles, roles, and sharing apart. Try to score at least 75% on two full practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Platform Foundations Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. The questions cover a range of basic Salesforce topics.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About one-third of the questions use short scenarios. They describe a business need and ask which object, cloud, or feature would help.
bestWayToPass: Learn the standard objects: Know what a Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Case represent.
Compare the clouds: Sales Cloud supports sales work, Service Cloud supports customer service, and Marketing Cloud supports campaigns. Learn where Data 360 fits.
Review access controls: Understand who can log in, which objects and fields they can use, and which records they can see.
Know the ecosystem: Learn what AppExchange and Trailhead offer, and why teams use sandboxes before changing production.

expertInsight: This is an entry-level exam, but you still need to know Salesforce terms clearly. Questions may include several plausible choices. Spend time learning what each standard object stores and what each cloud is used for; that will help you recognize the best answer.

certificationCard.description: This entry-level exam is for people with some Salesforce experience. It covers platform navigation, standard objects, reports and dashboards, security, and Salesforce products. The exam is 40 scored questions in 70 minutes, with a 62% pass mark, weighted towards Salesforce Ecosystem (32%) and Navigation (28%).

keyConcepts.h2: Salesforce Platform Foundations: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: How the Salesforce Platform Works
blocks.body: Salesforce is a cloud platform used by many customers. This shared model is called **multi-tenant**. Each customer works in a separate **org**, where their data is kept apart. Salesforce releases platform updates three times a year, in Spring, Summer, and Winter. Most changes are made in **Setup** without writing code. A **sandbox** is a copy of an org for building and testing changes. After testing, teams can move those changes to the live org, called **production**.

blocks.heading: Objects, Records, and Fields
blocks.body: Salesforce stores information in **objects**, much like tables in a database. A **record** is one item in an object, and a **field** stores one piece of information about that item. Common **standard objects** include **Lead** for a potential customer who is not yet qualified, **Account** for a company or person you work with, **Contact** for a person linked to an account, **Opportunity** for a potential sale, and **Case** for a customer issue. You can create **custom objects** for information that standard objects do not cover. **Relationships** connect records. A **lookup** is a flexible link; with **master-detail**, the child record depends on its parent and inherits its record access. Converting a Lead creates an Account and Contact, and can also create an Opportunity.

blocks.heading: How Access Is Controlled
blocks.body: Salesforce access has several layers. Login settings decide whether and when someone can sign in. A **profile** and any **permission sets** control which objects and fields they can use and what actions they can take. Record access is managed separately. The **org-wide default** sets the starting access for each object; the **role hierarchy** and **sharing rules** can give users access to more records. In short, profiles and permission sets control what users can do, while record sharing controls which records they can do it to.

blocks.heading: Automation and Reports
blocks.body: **Flow Builder** automates work such as updating records, sending emails, and guiding users through a process. **Validation rules** prevent records with invalid data from being saved. **Approval processes** send records to people for review. A **report** lists or summarizes records using a report type. A **dashboard** displays report information as charts and metrics. **List views** show a filtered set of records on an object tab. For this exam, focus on which tool fits each need.

blocks.heading: The Salesforce Ecosystem
blocks.body: **AppExchange** is Salesforce’s marketplace for apps and components. Some are free and some are paid, and they can be installed in an org. **Trailhead** is Salesforce’s free learning site, with lessons, trails, badges, and hands-on **Superbadges**. The **Trailblazer Community** is a place to ask questions and share solutions. Learn the main product families and their general purpose: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud, Tableau, MuleSoft, Slack, and Data 360.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Platform Foundations Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Many questions ask you to identify a Salesforce term or choose a feature for a simple business need. Learn the feature names and their purposes.

blocks.heading: Core Data Model
blocks.body: Review Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Case. Understand lookup and master-detail relationships, and know what happens when you convert a Lead.

blocks.heading: Automation
blocks.body: Use Flow Builder to automate steps, validation rules to prevent invalid data, and approval processes to request sign-off.

blocks.heading: Users and Access
blocks.body: Profiles and permission sets control actions on objects and fields. Org-wide defaults, roles, and sharing rules control access to records.

blocks.heading: Reports and Dashboards
blocks.body: Reports list or summarize records. Dashboards display report data visually. List views show filtered records on an object tab.

blocks.heading: Salesforce Products and Tools
blocks.body: AppExchange offers apps, Trailhead offers learning, and sandboxes let teams test changes before putting them in production. Salesforce releases platform updates three times a year.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Associate
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on your platform foundations knowledge with these related Salesforce credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: Who is the Salesforce Associate certification for?
options: People with up to six months of Salesforce experience
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Associate certification is for people who may have up to six months of experience using Salesforce.
whyWrong: The certification is for a broad audience, not developers alone.
This entry-level certification is not only for architects.
It is for general Salesforce users, not only marketers.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Customer 360 Platform mean?
options: Salesforce products working together to connect customer data across an organization
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer 360 is Salesforce’s connected set of products that brings customer data together across the organization.
whyWrong: Customer 360 includes more than Marketing Cloud.
Customer 360 includes more than Service Cloud.
Customer 360 includes more than Sales Cloud.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object is a central part of Salesforce’s CRM data model?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account is a core object for companies or people a business works with.
whyWrong: A Dashboard displays data; it is not a core CRM object.
A Report displays data; it is not a core CRM object.
An Email Template stores message content; it is not a core CRM object.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Salesforce record?
options: One row of data in an object, such as one Account
sampleQuestions.explanation: A record is one set of data in an object, like one Account.
whyWrong: A dashboard displays information; it is not one row of data.
A permission set controls access; it is not a data record.
A report type defines which data a report can use; it is not a record.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can users view their tasks and calendar in Salesforce?
options: The Home page and Activity components
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Home page and Activity components can show tasks and calendar information.
whyWrong: List views show records; they are not the only place to see tasks and calendar.
Dashboards show charts and metrics, not the task and calendar features described.
Reports display data but are not the only place to view activities.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Salesforce Dashboard?
options: A screen that displays several report charts and metrics together
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Dashboard brings several report charts and metrics together in one view.
whyWrong: A Dashboard can combine multiple report components.
An email template stores reusable email content.
A list view shows a filtered set of records, not several report components.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce feature lets users collaborate on records in real time?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Chatter and Activity support record collaboration through comments, mentions, and related interactions.
whyWrong: Validation Rules check data; they are not collaboration tools.
Workflow Rules automate actions; they are not real-time collaboration tools.
Reports display data; they do not provide the collaboration features described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Lightning Experience?
options: Salesforce’s modern user interface, with responsive design and newer features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lightning Experience is Salesforce’s modern user interface, designed to work across screen sizes and offer current features.
whyWrong: Classic is Salesforce’s older interface.
Lightning Experience is not limited to a mobile app.
An API connects systems; it is not a user interface.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object usually represents a company or person a business works with?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Account usually represents a company or person a business works with.
whyWrong: An Opportunity represents a potential sale.
A Task records work that someone needs to do.
A Report displays data; it does not represent a company or person.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Salesforce List View?
options: A table of records from one object, filtered by selected conditions
sampleQuestions.explanation: A List View shows a filtered set of records in a table.
whyWrong: A report type defines which records and fields a report can use.
A permission set controls what a user can access.
A Dashboard displays charts and metrics rather than a filtered record table.

sampleQuestions.question: Which navigation tools help users find apps and records in Salesforce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The App Launcher helps users open apps, and global search helps them find records and other content.
whyWrong: Workflow automates actions; it does not help users navigate or search.
Validation Rules check data; they do not help users navigate.
Report Builder creates reports; it is not the main app navigation or search tool.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the goal of the Customer 360 Platform?
options: A unified view of each customer across touchpoints and systems
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer 360 brings customer data together across products such as Sales and Service Cloud.
whyWrong: Customer 360 covers more than Service Cloud.
Customer 360 covers more than Marketing.
Customer 360 covers more than sales automation.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce feature lets users access Salesforce on phones and tablets?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce mobile app lets users work with Salesforce records on phones and tablets.
whyWrong: Reports alone do not provide the full mobile experience.
Email alone does not provide access to the full Salesforce app.
Salesforce also has a mobile app; it is not desktop-only.

sampleQuestions.question: What do Salesforce Reports do?
options: Organize, filter, and display data from Salesforce records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reports let users select, organize, filter, and display data from Salesforce records.
whyWrong: Sending email is not the purpose of Reports.
Reports do not assign tasks.
Reports can be used in Dashboards, but they also have their own purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce record represents a potential sale?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Opportunity represents a potential sale or deal the team is pursuing.
whyWrong: A Lead is a prospect who has not yet been qualified.
An Account represents a company or other organization.
A Contact represents a person.

sampleQuestions.question: What happens when a Lead gets converted?
options: It creates an Account and a Contact, and can also create an Opportunity
It deletes the Lead and creates nothing else
It only changes the Lead's status field
sampleQuestions.explanation: Converting a Lead turns it into an Account and a Contact, and optionally an Opportunity if there's a deal to track.
whyWrong: Converting keeps the record, it doesn't just delete it.
A status change alone isn't a conversion, conversion creates new records.
A Case tracks a customer issue, it isn't part of Lead conversion.

sampleQuestions.question: Which two things together control what a Salesforce user can do and see?
options: Profiles and permission sets control actions, record sharing controls which records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Profiles and permission sets decide what objects, fields, and actions a user has. Org-wide defaults, roles, and sharing rules separately decide which individual records they can reach.
whyWrong: The Role Hierarchy only affects record access, not what actions a user can take.
A password controls login, not what the user can do once signed in.
Dashboards and reports display data, they don't control access.

sampleQuestions.question: A team wants to stop records from saving unless a required field is filled in. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A validation rule checks a record against a condition and blocks the save with an error message if it fails.
whyWrong: A dashboard displays data, it doesn't block a save.
A list view filters which records show in a list, it has no effect on saving.
A permission set grants access, it doesn't check field values on save.

sampleQuestions.question: Before changing something in a live Salesforce org, a team wants to build and test it safely first. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sandbox is a copy of the org used to build and test changes before moving them to production.
whyWrong: A dashboard just displays report data, it isn't an environment for testing changes.
A report organizes and displays records, it isn't a testing environment.
A queue holds records for a team to work from, it has nothing to do with testing changes.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to install a pre-built app into their Salesforce org instead of building it from scratch. Where would they look?
sampleQuestions.explanation: AppExchange is Salesforce's marketplace for installable apps and components, free and paid.
whyWrong: Trailhead is Salesforce's free learning site, it doesn't host installable apps.
The Trailblazer Community is a forum for questions and discussion, not an app marketplace.
Setup is where an admin configures the org, it isn't where you find apps to install.
